paper_title: Efficient Polymer Solar Cells with a High Open Circuit Voltage of 1 Volt
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Adv Funct Materials - 2012 - Yuan - Efficient Polymer Solar Cells with a High Open Circuit Voltage of 1 Volt/auto/Adv Funct Materials - 2012 - Yuan - Efficient Polymer Solar Cells with a High Open Circuit Voltage of 1 Volt.md

knowledge_points.content: The PBDT-T-TPD polymer series incorporates alkylthienyl side chains onto the benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b']dithiophene (BDT) unit to replace original alkoxy side chains, aiming to improve coplanarity, broaden absorption, and deepen the HOMO energy level.
knowledge_points.evidence: Herein, we report a further improvement of their fill factor (FF), Voc, and PCE by incorporating three different alkylthienyl side chains to the BDT unit to replace the original alkoxy side chains. The introduction of conjugated thienyl side chains enhances the coplanarity of the polymer and may consequently lead to a broader absorption, higher charge mobilities and deeper HOMO.

knowledge_points.content: A polymer solar cell based on PBDT-T8-TPD and PC61BM achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 6.17%, a short-circuit current (Jsc) of 9.79 mA/cm², a fill factor (FF) of 63.0%, and an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 1.00 V.
knowledge_points.evidence: with optimal side chains, the tailored polymer demonstrated an increased FF, a high Voc of 1.00 V and a PCE of 6.17%... PT8 demonstrated a greatly increased FF (from 38.1% to 63.0%) and Jsc (from 5.90 to 9.79 mA/cm2).

knowledge_points.content: The topology of the alkyl side chains influences the polymer bandgap and HOMO levels; branched side chains (like 2-ethylhexyl in PT8) result in a more twisted backbone, a larger bandgap (~1.85 eV), and a deeper HOMO level (-5.61 eV) compared to linear side chains.
knowledge_points.evidence: From the CV measurement results, we concluded that polymer shows a larger bandgap and a deeper HOMO energy level when incorporating bulkier side chains... PT8 shows an apparently less broad absorption spectrum in CF and the absorption maximum is blue shifted. The introduction of bulkier side chains therefore increases the polymer bandgap.

knowledge_points.content: Hole mobilities in the PBDT-T-TPD series correlate with backbone coplanarity, where the most planar polymer (PT10) exhibits the highest mobility (7.9 x 10^-5 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹) and the most twisted (PT8) exhibits the lowest (5.9 x 10^-5 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹).
knowledge_points.evidence: The hole mobilities of T8, T12, and T10 pure film are 5.9 × 10−5, 7.0 × 10−5, and 7.9 × 10−5 cm2 V−1 s−1, respectively. These results indicate that higher polymer coplanarity is beneficial for charge transport.

knowledge_points.content: The use of 3% (v/v) 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO) as a solvent additive in chloroform significantly enhances the photovoltaic performance of PBDT-T8-TPD by improving polymer-fullerene phase separation and intermolecular packing.
knowledge_points.evidence: PT8 processed with DIO exhibited fine phase separation domains, leading to a more efficient charge transport... PT8 demonstrated a greatly increased FF (from 38.1% to 63.0%) and Jsc (from 5.90 to 9.79 mA/cm2) after the addition of DIO.

knowledge_points.content: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) imaging revealed that the addition of DIO to PBDT-T8-TPD:PC61BM blends transforms the film morphology from a smooth state to a network of interconnected polymer nanofibers.
knowledge_points.evidence: For PT8, after the addition of DIO, the morphology showed a dramatic change from the original smooth film to a network structured film with interconnected polymer nanofibers, which is the desired morphology for efficient carrier transport.

knowledge_points.content: PBDT-T-TPD polymers exhibit high thermal stability with 5% weight-loss temperatures (Td) exceeding 420 °C, attributed to the incorporation of alkylthienyl side chains.
knowledge_points.evidence: all the copolymers show good thermal stability under nitrogen atmosphere with the 5% weight-loss temperature (Td) at 423, 442, and 432 °C for PT8, PT10, and PT12, respectively. The excellent thermal stability is consistent with the previous reports that the incorporation of alkylthienyl side chains is helpful to improve polymer thermal stability.

knowledge_points.content: Density functional theory (DFT) and molecular mechanics simulations quantify polymer planarity using the standard deviation of Y coordinates (Y_StDev); PT10 is the most planar (0.695 Å) while PT8 is the most twisted (1.463 Å).
knowledge_points.evidence: The calculated standard deviations of Y coordinates of each atom (defined as Y_StDev) for PT8, PT12, and PT10 are 1.463, 1.181, and 0.695 Å, respectively (Figure 3a-d). We can see that PT10 shows the best planarity and PT8 shows the worst planarity.

knowledge_points.content: PBDT-T-TPD polymers are designed as large-bandgap materials to replace P3HT in tandem solar cells because they offer a similar bandgap but significantly higher open-circuit voltage (Voc) due to their deeper HOMO levels.
knowledge_points.evidence: The new copolymer has a similar bandgap to P3HT but shows a significantly improved Voc and PCE, making it a better candidate than P3HT for use as a large-bandgap material in tandem solar cells.

knowledge_points.content: Solubility differences between the polymers affect their response to additives; PT12 and PT10 show less morphology improvement with DIO compared to PT8 because they form rigid-rod aggregates in solution due to limited solubility.
knowledge_points.evidence: For PT12 and PT10, the improvement of photovoltaic performance is less pronounced... partially due to the limited solubility, PT12 and PT10 do not adapt the regular coil-like structure in solution, but adopt a similar rigid-rod conformation as in film... well-packed aggregates have already formed in solution state.
